newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: CNA SHARE RISES AMID RESTRUCTURING TALK.
newsitem.headline: CNA SHARE RISES AMID RESTRUCTURING TALK.

text.p: Shares in South African retail and entertainment group CNA Gallo Ltd rose on Wednesday on the back of the company's announcement that it was still assessing a restructuring of the firm, dealers said.
By about 0924 GMT the CNA stock added 10 cents to 350 cents with 1.6 million shares worth around 5.9 million rand exchanging hands.
"They had a cautionary this morning that the company is still busy with the restructuring move and I will say this is why the share is moving up," one dealer said.
The dealers said market players percieved the restructuring move to be positive in unlocking profit growth for the firm.
"The (CNA Gallo) guys are talking about the separate listing of the retail business and their (entertainment) business.
"I think the move will be positive for the company and I think that's why the share is going a little bit better," a dealer added.

CNA Gallo said on May 27 that a merchant bank was assessing ways to restructure the group to enable it to capitalise on its entertainment operations, which have overtaken the retail division in contribution to earnings.

The company's retail division recently reported headline earnings for the year ended March 31, of 27.7 million rand -- 28 percent down from 38.4 million rand the previous year -- while the entertainment division peaked its earnings by 53 percent to 37.8 million rand from 24.8 million rand.
